context: Decide and record: (1) mint a non-empty default machine_id_salt for new captures of retained fields only, and/or (2) one-time re-derive of retained-field values that deliberately breaks fixed-point for empty-salt tokens only. Prefer documenting accepted residual risk if operators choose keep-empty-salt. Never write recovered plaintext into tracker/PR bodies — tokens only.
description: ADR adr-published-identifier-field-set.md drops six unread fields but keeps publishing pseudonyms for endpoint, database_name, and submission_path, leaving the salt question open. After the field-drop re-derive (PR #1578), residual empty-salt tokens remain under retained keys (measured: database_5d7b725135a6 under database_name on sqlite corpus bundles). Dictionary confirmation against the public transform still works for those retained fields. The #1512 fixed point (already-public-shaped pseudonyms pass through) means minting a default salt alone does not rewrite stored corpus bytes; a deliberate re-hash policy for already-public tokens or a one-time migration of retained fields is required if stored tokens must change.
